feedback: This candidate changes three things from the iteration 2 design (score 625.2, the best raced so far): sensor y 0.07 to 0.08 (the contract maximum), kd 0.8 to 1.0, and base_speed 1.2 to 1.1. kp 4.5, ki 0.02, the sensor x spread, weights, wheel geometry, sensor_size and line_loss are unchanged, so the effect of these three changes is isolated. All values are inside the contract ranges. Iteration 2 showed the oval finishing 20/20 at 2.06 s and the s-bend finishing 15/20, with every failure off_track. The slalom finished 0/20, with every run ending off_track at progress about 0.36. Iteration 1 to 2 showed that moving the sensors forward and widening the spread paid off (185 to 625), so more sensing lead is the direction to keep pushing. Iteration 2 also showed steering_oscillation of 0.35 on the s-bend and control_effort of 12.8, so the robot is correcting hard. The kd increase is meant to damp the stronger corrections that the extra lead produces. The base_speed reduction gives steering margin on tight bends. The cost is time: at 1.1 the oval should still finish under 3 s, but with less slack than at 1.2. I cannot judge the outcome from numbers, so this should be read from the race. Read these first: completion_time on the oval, whether the slalom produces any completions, max_error and line_loss_events on the slalom and s-bend, and steering_oscillation. If the slalom still leaves at low progress with max_error near 0.06, steering authority is the limit: raise kp to about 5.0 before adding more lead, since sensor y is already at its maximum. If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.4, lower kd to about 0.8 before touching kp. If the oval completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, return base_speed toward 1.2.
requested_changes: If the slalom still ends off_track at progress below 0.5 with max_error near 0.06, raise kp from 4.5 to 5.0 and keep sensor y at 0.08, because the sensor position is already at its maximum (iteration 2 slalom progress 0.36).
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 (iteration 2 s-bend was 0.35 with kd 0.8), reduce kd from 1.0 to 0.8 before changing kp.
If the oval completion_time exceeds 2.5 s or the oval fails to finish, return base_speed to 1.2, the iteration 2 value that gave 2.06 s finishes on the oval.
